rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a foundational multimodal configuration to establish baseline performance. This experiment tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, which clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modal baselines. It is the best use of the first experiment as it directly addresses the core hypothesis of multimodal value.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (concat fusion) achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_017) improves performance, directly clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. Since fusion is a critical design choice with limited prior evidence, this comparison is highly informative under the budget constraint.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.52 accuracy, but aggregation method (None vs avgpool) remains untested. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation for multiprofile, clarifying whether aggregation methods impact performance. It balances exploration of critical design choices (aggregation) while building on prior multimodal success.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and concat fusion (e.g., config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests whether upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful architecture) further improves performance while keeping other components (pca_n2000 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, concat fusion) consistent. This clarifies the impact of the image encoder on performance, a critical design choice, without deviating from the proven effective configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and pca_n2000 perform best (config_024/025). This experiment tests transformer aggregation (vs avgpool in config_025) with weighted fusion, clarifying whether aggregation method impacts performance. It builds on the top-performing configuration while exploring a key design choice with potential to improve accuracy.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_024, accuracy 0.6287) outperforms resnet50, and avgpool aggregation (config_018, 0.6186) is better than transformer. This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat (config_024) to weighted (config_025) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion methods. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion type) in a high-performing configuration, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether replacing the pca_n2000 RNA encoder with scvi_n200 in this high-performing setup improves accuracy, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice while maintaining other effective components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and multiprofile setting achieve high validation accuracy (config_037: 0.706). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (used in config_037) could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of aggregation methods on model effectiveness. It balances exploitation of promising components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) with exploration of aggregation strategies.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders, using transformer aggregation, achieve high accuracy (config_038: 0.7207). This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted in this promising setup clarifies if fusion method is a critical factor. It directly addresses an important design choice with potential to improve performance while building on prior success.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while maintaining the same aggregation/fusion strategy (transformer + weighted) improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of high-performing patterns and exploration of critical design decisions under limited budget.
